title: AI is upending Boston-area tech businesses, amid buyouts and job cuts
key_facts: On Monday 5 Oct 2026, PTC, a Boston industrial design software firm whose stock had fallen on fears of AI displacement, drew a takeover offer from France's Schneider Electric of $205 a share, if the deal is completed.
On Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, HubSpot, a Cambridge business software firm, said it would cut nearly 700 jobs as it struggles with AI competition.
HubSpot's chief executive Yamini Rangan wrote to employees: 'This is not simply a cost-cutting exercise'; departing staff get 20 to 30 weeks of severance.
On Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, Amazon said it will sublease more than half of its Seaport office tower in Boston.
Waltham robotics company Boston Dynamics hired former Amazon AI leader Rohit Prasad as its new chief executive.
An analyst at William Blair says job cutting is widespread among software companies adding AI features while their stock prices sink.
quote_evidence: “This is not simply a cost-cutting exercise,” Rangan wrote in an email to employees.
“Tech has always been about cycles and whether it’s dot com, mobile, or now AI,” Boston VC Greg Raiz said.
why_it_matters_hint: AI pressure on software firms is driving job cuts and takeovers in Boston, though the local effect may be muted.
